ServiceProvider? ServiceProvider = new ServiceCollection().AddCanisterModules()?.BuildServiceProvider(); // Get our cache provider. Cache? CacheProvider = ServiceProvider?.GetService<Cache>(); if (CacheProvider is null) return; // Get our cache. This will create a new cache if one doesn't exist with the name "Default". ICache? Cache = CacheProvider.GetOrAddCache(); if (Cache is null) return; // Add our data to the cache. _ = Cache.Set("Test", new ExampleClass { A = 12 }); // Check if our data is in the cache and retrieve it. Console.WriteLine("Data found: {0}", Cache.TryGetValue("Test", out ExampleClass value)); Console.WriteLine("Our stored data: {0}", value.A); } } } Output Data found: True Our stored data: 12

index.html.title: DragonHoard | DragonHoard API Reference
index.html.summary: DragonHoard DragonHoard is a .NET in-memory caching library with a small API for storing, retrieving, expiring, and grouping cached values. Choose its lightweight in-memory provider or a provider backed by Microsoft.Extensions.Caching.Memory. Why DragonHoard? Register caches through Microsoft.Extensions.DependencyInjection. Create named caches for separate workloads. Set absolute or sliding expiration, priority, size, and tags per entry. Retrieve or remove entries by key or tag, and compact a cache when needed. Target .NET 8, .NET 9, and .NET 10. DragonHoard is an in-process cache. It does not persist entries or synchronize them between application instances. Choose a provider Install one provider package for your application. Both include the core API as a dependency. Provider NuGet package Use when DragonHoard in-memory DragonHoard.InMemory You want DragonHoard's built-in in-memory cache. Microsoft memory cache DragonHoard.Microsoft.Extensions.Caching.Memory You want DragonHoard's API backed by Microsoft.Extensions.Caching.Memory. Install Install the provider you chose with the .NET CLI: dotnet add package DragonHoard.InMemory Or install the Microsoft memory cache provider: dotnet add package DragonHoard.Microsoft.Extensions.Caching.Memory Quick start This example registers the in-memory provider, creates the default cache, and stores and retrieves a value. Replace AddInMemoryHoard() with AddMemoryCacheHoard() to use the Microsoft memory cache provider. using DragonHoard.Core; using DragonHoard.Core.Interfaces; using Microsoft.Extensions.DependencyInjection; var services = new ServiceCollection(); services.AddInMemoryHoard(); using var serviceProvider = services.BuildServiceProvider(); var cacheManager = serviceProvider.GetRequiredService<Cache>(); var cache = cacheManager.GetOrAddCache()!; cache.Set("greeting", "Hello, cache!"); if (cache.TryGetValue<string>("greeting", out var greeting)) { Console.WriteLine(greeting); } The Cache manager is registered as a singleton. It provides access to the default cache and additional named caches. Resolve it through dependency injection rather than creating a new manager for each operation. Common operations Create a named cache Use a descriptive name to keep unrelated data in separate caches: ICache productCache = cacheManager.GetOrAddCache("products")!; Set expiration and tags cache.Set("product:42", product, new CacheEntryOptions { AbsoluteExpirationRelativeToNow = TimeSpan.FromMinutes(10), Tags = ["products", "featured"] }); Entries can also use AbsoluteExpiration, SlidingExpiration, Priority, and Size options. The in-memory provider supports capacity and scan-frequency configuration through AddInMemoryHoard: services.AddInMemoryHoard(options => { options.MaxCacheSize = 10_000; options.ScanFrequency = TimeSpan.FromMinutes(2); }); Remove or retrieve entries cache.Remove("product:42"); bool found = cache.TryGetValue<Product>("product:42", out var product); cache.RemoveByTag("featured"); Product[] featuredProducts = cache.GetByTag<Product>("featured"); Compact a cache Compact removes a fraction of entries according to the provider's eviction policy. For DragonHoard's in-memory provider, expired entries are removed first; remaining entries are considered from lowest to highest priority, then by expiration and last-access time. cache.Compact(0.25); // Ask the provider to remove about 25% of its entries. Expiration and provider behavior Expiration and eviction details depend on the provider. The in-memory provider uses a one-minute scan frequency by default. Expired values should not be treated as available after expiration, but background cleanup timing can depend on cache activity. Compact also follows the selected provider's eviction policy. Develop and test The repository contains the library, an example application, tests, and BenchmarkDotNet benchmarks. A .NET 10 SDK is needed to build and test the full solution; the library packages target .NET 8, .NET 9, and .NET 10. git clone https://github.com/JaCraig/DragonHoard.git cd DragonHoard dotnet build DragonHoard.sln dotnet test DragonHoard.sln Run the example or benchmarks with: dotnet run --project DragonHoard.Example dotnet run -c Release --project DragonHoard.Benchmarks Benchmark results depend on the machine, runtime, and workload. Run the benchmarks yourself to compare current results rather than relying on historical numbers.
